firms.name: FTMO
firms.notes: Challenge fees are charged in EUR by default, though you can pick a USD, GBP or other trading-account currency. Founded in 2015 in the Czech Republic and widely considered legitimate. Not a regulated broker. Traders report sudden account bans after payouts and disputes over stop-loss and timezone execution. FTMO acquired the regulated broker OANDA in December 2025. That is separate from its own challenge product.

secondaryReview.note: FPA is known for being tougher on prop firms than Trustpilot — a consistent 4.4 there corroborates the Trustpilot number rather than contradicting it.

firms.name: The5%ers
firms.notes: Shown: a flat $74 fee per account, scaling to $100k to $125k on performance. The firm runs several programmes (Bootcamp, Pro Growth, High Stakes, Hyper Growth) with different payout terms, so check the one you're considering. Traders report payout denials and account terminations citing vague 'integrity concerns', often after profitable trades. ForexPeaceArmy found a paid campaign to post fake positive reviews and rates the firm zero stars, so treat its high Trustpilot score with caution. Flagged as unregulated by WikiFX.

externalReview.note: Review-count figures vary widely by source (17k-34k as of Aug 2026); treated as approximate. See manipulation warning below — this score should not be taken at face value.

secondaryReview.note: FPA set this firm's rating to zero stars after finding a paid campaign encouraging fake positive reviews — a direct contradiction of its high Trustpilot score.

firms.name: FundedNext
firms.notes: Shown: the Stellar 1-Step challenge. Other challenge types have different rules. The futures Bolt and Rapid challenges were retired for new buyers in July 2026. EA trading is allowed on Stellar forex and CFD accounts for a separate fee. Strategies must be customised, identical copy trading across accounts is banned, and there is a $300k cap per EA. EAs are not supported on cTrader. Shown prices are base prices; promo codes are common. Traders report refused refunds and an undisclosed 3.5% payout processing fee. ForexPeaceArmy found fake 5-star reviews traced to a company employee's IP address.

externalReview.note: Sources vary 62k-75k reviews; treated as approximate. See manipulation warning below — some of this firm's positive review volume has been directly traced to fake accounts.

secondaryReview.note: No clean aggregate score — FPA's review thread documents fake 5-star reviews traced to FundedNext's own Partner Manager IP address.

firms.name: Apex Trader Funding
firms.notes: Availability: Apex does not accept South African residents, according to restricted-country lists. Pricing: Apex moved to a one-time evaluation fee in March 2026. The costs shown are the old monthly rates and are out of date, and the rules shown also reflect the pre-March 2026 model. Futures and indices only. Traders report payout denials and account freezes. A federal lawsuit, Lawton v. Apex Trader Funding (W.D. Texas, filed July 2026), alleges fraudulent practices; Apex denies the claims. Earlier matters include an $800k dispute between two traders, attorney-general complaints in Michigan and Texas, and a gag-order lawsuit against a YouTuber. Metals trading has been suspended since March 2026.

externalReview.note: Trustpilot skews positive because reviews are often left right after funding, before payout disputes surface — see our complaint research in the notes above. About 8.7% of Trustpilot reviews are 1-star, describing slow payouts, account closures after becoming profitable, and support going silent.

secondaryReview.note: FPA's review thread contains detailed trader complaints about payout restrictions and rule enforcement — consistent with our own lawsuit/complaint findings above despite the decent aggregate Trustpilot number.

firms.name: E8 Markets (E8 Funding)
firms.notes: Shown: the E8 One default profile. Other products (E8 Zero, Pro and Signature) have different rules, so check each one. E8 One's funded stage has a 5-minute blackout around high-impact news. Weekend holding is allowed on E8 One but not on E8 Signature forex and crypto, which close positions daily at 23:00 server time. Rebranded from E8 Funding in November 2023. A $500k payout dispute happened before the rebrand. Recent reviews mostly complain about rule complexity and funded-account processing times rather than missed payouts.

secondaryReview.note: Generally positive on FPA too — fast payouts and responsive support are recurring themes, though some traders report rules (like leverage) changing immediately after passing a challenge.

firms.name: Topstep
firms.notes: Futures and indices only. The Trading Combine is a monthly subscription ($49, $99 or $199) plus a $149 activation fee on funding. Consistency rule: no single day can make up more than 50% of the profit target, and a day only counts toward progress if net profit clears $150. Max drawdown is $2,000 on $50k, $3,000 on $100k and $4,500 on $150k; the 3% shown reflects the larger tiers. EAs are allowed during the evaluation, but funded TopstepX accounts prohibit fully automated EAs, bots and trade copiers. Since January 2026 new accounts get a 90/10 split from the first dollar. Named in a federal lawsuit (McCrudden v. Topstep, filed April 2026) alleging shifting rules and inaccessible profit reserves; no ruling found. Eleven platform outages in late 2025 caused forced liquidations, and BBB complaints rose sharply in the same period. The firm has taken legal action against a public critic.

externalReview.note: Down from 3.5 ("Average") last cycle — the lowest Trustpilot score of any active firm in this comparison, consistent with the 2025 outages, tripled BBB complaints, and active lawsuit above.

firms.name: True Forex Funds
firms.notes: Permanently shut down in May 2024, after MetaQuotes terminated its MT4 and MT5 licence in February 2024 and the firm declared insolvency. About $1.2M in trader payouts, roughly 300 traders, remains unpaid. No relaunch or successor has been found.

firms.name: Blue Guardian
firms.notes: Shown: base price before promo codes, which often cut it by 30 to 60 percent. Phase 1 profit target 8%, Phase 2 4%. Funded profit split is 85%; 90% needs a paid add-on. On accounts bought after 13 November 2025, trades opened or closed within 5 minutes of high-impact news are not allowed on funded accounts. Owned by Iconic Exchange FZCO (Dubai), founded 2021. Its 2024 broker acquisition, Guardian Markets, is listed under that name on Trustpilot. Traders report automatic closes at a 1 to 2% floating loss, ignored stop-losses, payout denials after earlier payouts, and accounts terminated for 'shared device' or 'ban evasion'. An April 2026 forum thread alleged software was used to trigger breaches.

externalReview.note: Ratings vary unusually widely by platform (3.6 here vs 4.1-4.8 reported elsewhere) — treat any single number with caution. Trustpilot now displays this listing under the business name "Guardian Markets" (see notes above).

secondaryReview.note: Contains a detailed complaint from a profitable trader whose account was breached and access refused even after support acknowledged unauthorized activity, plus an Apr 2026 thread alleging software-triggered breaches — worth reading before purchasing.

firms.name: Fidelcrest
firms.notes: Shut down in March 2024, apparently as an exit scam. It kept taking challenge payments, refused refunds to traders in good standing, then stopped responding. No relaunch or successor has been found. Some review sites still list it as active; those listings are out of date. Not recommended.

firms.name: City Traders Imperium
firms.notes: EAs are allowed only if you can prove you own the source code. Third-party black-box bots and automated news scalping are prohibited. First payout after 7 profitable days and 2% profit, then monthly on 1-Step and 2-Step (every two weeks on Instant Funding). The 70% split shown rises toward 100% with a longer funded track record. Operating since 2018 with a large claimed payout total. Traders report payout denials tied to copy trading and high-risk rule enforcement. No scam pattern found. Pricing and minimum trading-day rules may have changed, so check the firm's site before buying.

secondaryReview.note: Only 2 reviews on FPA — too small a sample to mean much on its own, shown mainly because it doesn't contradict the Trustpilot picture.

firms.name: Lux Trading Firm
firms.notes: Priced in GBP. Shown: the 1-Step evaluation sizes (£199, £449, £999). Fixed 6% max drawdown with no trailing. The daily loss limit is not shown; confirm it and the reset fee on the firm's site, since sources disagree. Not regulated by the FCA, ASIC or any other financial regulator. Traders report few confirmed payouts and recurring withdrawal delays. Not the same firm as Lucid Trading or Luxemarkets, which reviews sometimes confuse with it.

externalReview.note: Review counts reported elsewhere range from ~400 to ~650 — low enough volume that this figure moves a lot per new review, unlike the larger firms in this list.

secondaryReview.note: Only 1 review on FPA (2 stars) — not enough data to draw a conclusion from, but it doesn't support the Trustpilot picture either.

firms.name: MyForexFunds
firms.notes: Not accepting new challenge purchases. The CFTC case against parent company Traders Global Group was dismissed with prejudice in May 2025, after the CFTC was found to have misled the court. A Canadian receivership has wound down. A February 2026 commitment to pay verified August 2023 claims is in progress. The company is still reviewing its operations before deciding whether to relaunch. A claim of a new product launch has no credible coverage behind it. Not recommended until a relaunch is credibly confirmed.
